coverage_summary: Reviewed all six supplied trajectories against the paper text. The unconditional prompt/tokenization paths are largely supported, but important tasks, lifecycle routes, training operands, preprocessing, and generation postprocessing are missing.

findings.detail: The document represents only unconditional generation. The paper defines conditional cell sentence generation and cell type prediction as additional tasks, with distinct prompt inputs and outputs. These routes are absent for the represented models and phases.

evidence.quote:
1. Unconditional cell sentence generation: produce a sequence of 100 genes without any prescribed cell type label.
2. Conditional cell sentence generation: generate a sequence of 100 genes given a specific cell type label.
3. Cell type prediction: generate a cell type label following a provided sequence of 100 genes.

For conditional cell generation and unconditional cell generation used in our experiments from Section 2.2, we randomly sample prompt templates as input, inserting the cell type where needed for conditional generation. For autoregressive cell type prediction, we randomly sample templates as in training but use either real cell sentences from our test dataset or generated cell sentences.

findings.required_change: Add the conditional-generation and autoregressive cell-type-prediction trajectories, including their documented prompt operands, branches, and outputs.

findings.detail: There are no inference trajectories for GPT-2 Medium, although the paper trains four GPT-2 models and describes inference for the trained models. The supplied graph contains only GPT-2 Small inference routes.

evidence.quote: We train four GPT-2 models [26] on a corpus of cell sentences sampled from [39].
At inference, we follow the training procedure in Section 3.2 (see Figures 1, 2, and 6).

findings.required_change: Add GPT-2 Medium inference trajectories for the applicable model variants and tasks.

findings.detail: The graph starts with an already formed cell_sentence and omits the documented source transformations: filtering, quality-control selection, row normalization to 10,000 counts, log normalization, rank ordering, and truncation to the top 100 genes. The node also uses an unconstrained n_ranked_genes shape despite the explicit top-100 training representation.

evidence.quote: We follow standard preprocessing steps for single-cell RNA seq data, including filtering cells with fewer than 200 genes expressed and filtering genes which are expressed in fewer than 200 cells. Quality control metrics are then calculated based on mitochondrial gene counts within each cell using the Scanpy Python library [48], and low-quality cells are filtered out which contain over 2500 counts, or which have greater than 20 percent of transcript counts from mitochondrial genes. The count matrix is then row-normalized so that each cell sums up to 10,000 transcript counts and then log-normalized [49]
In order to limit computational costs, we truncate each cell sentence to only keep the 100 highest expressed (top 100 ranked) genes.

findings.required_change: Represent or explicitly bound the documented preprocessing and rank/top-100 transformation, and set the cell-sentence instance to the documented 100-gene form.

findings.detail: The cell_sentence training target is present as a disconnected node, while the model boundary receives only prompt_tokens. The paper documents task-associated outputs and different loss scopes for pretraining and fine-tuning, but the assembly preserves neither a target/label operand nor an explicit unresolved target boundary.

evidence.quote: The prompt structure for cell type prediction combines the prompt with the cell sentence . For conditional cell generation, it merges the prompt with the specified cell type . In contrast, the unconditional cell generation prompt primarily consists of a succinct directive
Unlike for our pretraining setup, we apply the instruction fine-tuning task in a classical manner, computing the loss exclusively on labels.

findings.required_change: Connect the documented training target/label to the training boundary, or retain an explicit unresolved target interface without asserting whether it is appended to the prompt or supplied separately.

findings.detail: The pretraining tokenizer invocation records a BPE vocabulary trained on the relevant corpus but omits the documented vocabulary size of 9,609 tokens.

evidence.quote: We train a Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer [51] on the full cell sentence dataset, including NL prompts and cell type labels, yielding a vocabulary of 9,609 tokens.

findings.required_change: Record the documented vocabulary size as an invocation/resource parameter for the pretraining tokenizer paths.

findings.detail: The sampling invocation identifies top-p/top-k sampling but omits the explicitly reported values top_p=0.95 and top_k=50.

evidence.quote: We set the hyperparameters top_p = 0 . 95 and top_k = 50 to promote diversity in cell generation.

findings.required_change: Record top_p=0.95 and top_k=50 in the sampling invocation.

findings.detail: The inference chain has no EOS-controlled stopping branch. Its generated_tokens output therefore does not preserve the documented termination condition.

evidence.quote: All outputs are generated until an end-of-sequence (EOS) token is predicted, which was appended to all training samples.

findings.required_change: Represent EOS as the documented stopping condition on autoregressive generation/sampling, without inventing an unreported extraction rule.

findings.detail: The inference chain stops at generated_tokens and omits the documented post-generation regex extraction that removes prompts and extracts genes or cell-type labels. The same omission occurs in the fine-tuned inference path.

evidence.quote: Post-generation, gene and cell type extraction is done using regex to remove prompts.

findings.required_change: Add a documented post-generation extraction boundary or operation, preserving the regex implementation as unspecified where the paper gives no further detail.

findings.detail: The fine-tuned inference path also omits the documented EOS stopping condition and regex extraction boundary.

evidence.quote: All outputs are generated until an end-of-sequence (EOS) token is predicted, which was appended to all training samples. Post-generation, gene and cell type extraction is done using regex to remove prompts.

findings.required_change: Add EOS-controlled generation and the post-generation extraction boundary to the fine-tuned inference trajectory.
